stem.text: The process of ultrafiltration occurs in the Bowman’s capsule region of a kidney nephron.
Figure 7.1 is a diagram representing part of a Bowman’s capsule.

stem.caption: Figure 7.1
stem.alt: Part of the Bowman’s capsule with cells A and C and structure B labelled.

stem.text: State the name of cell A, structure B and cell C.

markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: The filtration barrier is arranged between capillary blood and the capsule lumen. Capillary endothelium is on the blood side; podocyte foot processes face the capsule space, with the basement membrane between them.

reasoningChain: Use position relative to each lumen to identify the two cells and intervening membrane.

stem.text: The kidney function of a person can be assessed by measuring the glomerular filtration rate (GFR). The GFR is the rate at which fluid filters from the blood in the glomerulus into the Bowman’s capsule.
Suggest factors that are likely to decrease the GFR.

points.text: dehydration / reduced water potential of blood / loss of blood / heart failure ;
damage to, Bowman’s capsule / basement membrane / glomerulus / arterioles ;
ref. to, drugs / hormones, qualified ; A named or action described e.g. ADH / beta blockers / diuretics

markScheme.note: Point n follows the order of the transcribed marking points; table rows or source labels such as 3a and 3b retain their original wording.

explanation.text: Filtration depends on the net pressure across a permeable filtration barrier. A factor may reduce the driving pressure, the available filtration surface or the permeability of the barrier.

reasoningChain: Consider blood supply and the filtration barrier separately.
Give three specified factors that could reduce filtration.

stem.text: The kidney has an important role in homeostasis.
Explain what is meant by the term homeostasis and describe the principles of homeostasis in mammals.

points.text: maintain constant internal environment / AW ; e.g. within narrow limits
despite changes in the, internal / external, environment ;

max two from:
named factor ; e.g. temperature / water potential / blood glucose concentration
changes in factor / stimulus, detected by (named) receptor ;
ref. to central control decision / AW ; e.g. ref. to, brain / CNS / hypothalamus
factor returns to, set point / norm ;

explanation.text: A control loop compares the detected condition with a reference value. The response reduces the original deviation; it is the direction of the correction, rather than merely the existence of a response, that makes feedback negative.

reasoningChain: Start with the maintained internal condition.
Trace stimulus, receptor, coordination and effector to restoration towards the set point.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Many responses correctly stated the relevant structures and processes.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Some responses confused endothelial and epithelial cells or mixed up A and C.
Some responses stated basal, instead of basement, membrane.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Many responses identified a range of different factors that are likely to decrease the GFR.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Some responses needs specificity with unqualified references to pressure or comparing the diameters of the afferent and efferent arterioles.
Some responses also included incorrect references to water potential and osmosis.

blocks.heading: Comprehensive responses
bullets: Some responses started with an accurate definition, followed by a logical outline of the principles of homeostasis using appropriate terminology which was then related to an appropriate example.

blocks.heading: Limited responses
bullets: Some responses focused on a described example, often omitting any information regarding receptors and effectors and using vague language, for example glucose or water levels rather than blood glucose concentration or blood water potential.
Some responses incorrectly referred to positive feedback.
Few responses stated that a constant internal environment is maintained despite changes in the internal environment.
